The claim states that Monocular Depth Consistency Loss enforces geometric consistency between a rendered depth map and dense depth priors from off-the-shelf networks, resolving scale ambiguity. Source [S1] explicitly mentions using off-the-shelf networks (ZoeDepth, DepthAnything) for dense per-pixel depth priors and addressing scale ambiguity by aligning them with sparse SfM points using scale and shift parameters. Source [S2] explicitly defines a 'monocular depth loss' ($L_{Mono}$) that enforces consistency between estimated depth ($ ar{D}$) and predicted monocular depth ($ ar{D}$) using a closed-form least-squares solution for scale ($ eta$) and shift ($epsilon$) parameters. Both sources confirm the use of off-the-shelf monocular networks, the enforcement of consistency via a specific loss function, and the resolution of scale/shift ambiguity.
